headline: {arm:atlas-m} costs {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} per thousand conversations against {arm:atlas-l}'s {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} and gives up a few points of overall quality; the two cheaper models give up far more, most on declining to speculate and confirming account changes.
lede: {arm:brisk-s} declines speculation bait {task.specul.brisk-s.declines.mean|pct} of the time, against {task.specul.atlas-m.declines.mean|pct} for {arm:atlas-m}. A guardrail floor near the Atlas models' level on that behaviour or on confirming account changes would rule out both cheap models, and a price per point of overall quality would settle {arm:atlas-m} against {arm:atlas-l}; neither was declared.
flag: Nothing was declared before the run: no control, no quality floor and no exchange rate between cost and quality. Code's dominance call names {arm:brisk-s} because it weighs cost alone; this page does not follow it, since no quality axis was declared for it to weigh.

caveats.material_if: only if the judge scores declining to speculate or confirming account changes differently by model; the cheap models' losses on those behaviours rest on it, while cost and latency are measured
only for the small gaps between Atlas-L and Atlas-M; the cheap models' gaps on the two guardrail behaviours are clear even on each model's own interval
only if production traffic is weighted so heavily toward one task that the quality gaps there decide alone; the cost order is the same in every task
only if a few points of the overall quality score is a large difference on a scale the input does not define

decision.text: {arm:atlas-l} scores highest on overall quality in every task and costs most. {arm:atlas-m} trails it by a few points at {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} per thousand conversations. {arm:open-70b} and {arm:brisk-s} cost least and lose most where a wrong reply does harm.

No price per point can be computed, because quality is stated per task only. A floor on declining to speculate or on confirming account changes set near {arm:atlas-m}'s level removes both cheap models. Between {arm:atlas-m} and {arm:atlas-l}, the call turns on whether a few points of overall quality are worth the cost gap.

Our lean, not a rule: {arm:atlas-m}. It is not separated from {arm:atlas-l} on any judged behaviour and costs far less. The lean holds while the owner accepts a few points of overall quality for that saving.

The concierge product owner declares floors on declining to speculate and confirming account changes, and a price per point of overall quality. With both, the four measured models rank without a judgment call.

Confirming before account changes was scored only in troubleshooting; billing & account questions hold no figure for it, so the cheap models' exposure where account changes are most common is unmeasured.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-l} scores highest on overall quality in every task and costs most; {arm:atlas-m} sits a few points lower at a fraction of the cost, and the two cheap models fall furthest in troubleshooting and research questions.

evidence.caption: Overall quality score against cost per thousand conversations, one panel per task, cost on a log scale. No quality line was declared.

claims.text: The cheap models lose most on the two behaviours where a wrong reply does harm. {arm:brisk-s} declines speculation bait {task.specul.brisk-s.declines.mean|pct} of the time. {arm:open-70b} confirms before account changes {task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean|pct} of the time. Neither interval reaches {arm:atlas-m}'s.

evidence.caption: Judged rate with its interval, per model. No floor was declared for either behaviour.

claims.text: On every other judged behaviour {arm:atlas-m} is not separated from {arm:atlas-l}, while {arm:brisk-s} trails most on resolving troubleshooting issues, at {task.trouble.brisk-s.resolves.mean|pct}.

evidence.caption: Judged rates with their intervals, per task and model. Each interval is the model's own, not a paired comparison.

claims.text: Latency rules no model out: every p95 sits under the {aspects.overall.bar.latency_s.atlas-l.bar} bar, the slowest being {arm:atlas-l} on research-needed questions at {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95}.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95, per task and model. The declared bar is stated in the sentence and not drawn.

explore.control: Floor on declining to speculate and on confirming before account changes
explore.outcome: A floor above the top of either cheap model's interval removes it. No floor reads Atlas-M and Atlas-L apart with confidence: their intervals overlap on both behaviours.

explore.control: Price of a point of overall quality, per thousand conversations
explore.binds: Atlas-M against Atlas-L, and both against the cheap models
explore.outcome: The flip point cannot be located: no model-level quality figure exists to price. Within each task, a higher price moves the choice toward Atlas-L.

explore.binds: each model's blended cost and quality
explore.outcome: The cost order is the same in every task, so the mix moves no cost ranking. It only weights the quality gaps, which are largest in troubleshooting and research questions.

omitted.why: It weighs cost alone because no quality axis was declared; the flag says so once, and the page does not follow it.

omitted.what: Open-70B's top in-character rate in persona small talk
omitted.why: Not separated from Atlas-L or Atlas-M; it changes no option's standing. It stays in the judged-behaviours chart and its table.
The cost order is the same in every task; the model-level costs carry the trade, and the per-task costs are in the cost-against-quality panels.

omitted.what: Latency medians and per-task tails beyond the slowest
omitted.why: Every model is well under the bar, so latency decides nothing; full figures stay in the latency chart and its table.

omitted.what: Scoreboard (cases run, none lost or failed)
omitted.why: Describes the method; one line in Method.

omitted.what: A routed mix (a cheap model on billing & account questions, where its overall quality is closest)
omitted.why: Nobody ran it, so no figure states its cost or quality; and speculation bait and account changes can arrive in any task, so routing by task does not avoid the cheap models' weak behaviours. Named as a next step only.

omitted.what: Price per point and monthly cost
omitted.why: No tool can state them: quality has no model-level figure and no monthly volume was declared.

next.text: The concierge product owner declares floors on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes.
next.settles: Whether Brisk-S and Open-70B stay on the table; at any floor near the Atlas models' level, the trade narrows to Atlas-M against Atlas-L.

next.text: Calibrate the judge with human ratings on speculation-bait and account-change replies from all four models.
next.settles: Turns the judge caveat into evidence for the two behaviours the cheap models' losses rest on.

next.text: Declare a price per point of overall quality, the traffic mix across tasks and a monthly volume.
next.settles: Lets the trade be priced at model level and decides Atlas-M against Atlas-L without a judgment call.

next.text: Score confirming before account changes on billing & account questions.
next.settles: Whether the cheap models' weakest behaviour also shows where account changes are most common.

next.text: If a cheaper option is still wanted, run a routed mix (a cheap model on billing & account questions, Atlas-M elsewhere) as a measured option, scoring speculation and account-change confirmation inside the routed traffic.
next.settles: Whether routing keeps the saving without the guardrail losses, so it can be priced beside the four measured models.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases|int} cases per model across the tasks; repeats are not stated. No trial was lost or failed.
Each is a pass or fail verdict from a judge whose model and calibration the input does not state. Each behaviour is scored in one task only.
An ordinal score per task; the input does not define its scale.
Each model's own interval per task, at the level each chart prints, neither paired nor corrected for the number of comparisons. Not separated means the intervals overlap; it never means equal.
Cost per thousand conversations, measured. No monthly volume was declared, so no monthly figure is stated.
p50 and p95 per task; one bar was declared, and every model met it.
No control was named, so no change against a control exists; quality has no model-level figure, and no traffic mix was declared.
